raidSayLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Colton Wieczorek. Zookeeper. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Knife roll, Dispatcher's headset, Home key, Unnamed photograph, Photo album. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night,
A person, maybe 30s: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
The drumbeat with no drummer stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. It's still out there.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
It stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. Something displaced a LOT of water is still out there.
Dale came back from the treeline white-faced. Saw it too. Whatever it is, it's still out there.
Something moves out there — a dog-shaped silence at the treeline.
It followed you. The dog-shaped silence at the treeline is here.
